So basically, you are promoting complete consolidation of the market with ONLY one negotiation that is possible: Hospital + Insurance companies.  

We know how it has been working out between the two of them - >15% year-to-year growth in costs? 

Force all physicians into complete dependency on hospitals; give hospitals "tyrannical" power over physicians.   Essentially, make employed + non-employed physicians equally dependent on hospital largesse.

Remove ANY incentive for health insurance to negotiate fair rates directly with physicians. 

We see where it's going - not a free market but Monopoly on hospital + physician services + Monopsony on insurer side.  

Instead of negotiating a fair compensation, you want to "force" physicians to sign whatever contract @UHC and @AnthemBCBS puts in front of their nose, often without even the right to read the contract.  You know well that there are no negotiatons and that's why 80% of physicians are "employed."

Brilliant idea.  Brookings institution is truly a "think tank" but it can think only "one step" at a time.  
Oblivious to unintended consequences.

If this was an attempt to report without bias, objectively, on an issue that creates a great headache for physicians + patients, this could have been a Pulitzer worthy article. 

Instead, the article is nothing but a political hit piece before elections. 

It fails to consider the reality, the physician/practice perspective. Have you considered the alternative? No OB-GYN when you need one?  Very common in many rural counties. 

How do you think medical practices can provide care to the low income patients if they don’t get paid?

Employees have to be paid.  
Rent has to be paid. 
Taxes have to be paid. 
Malpractice has to be paid. 
Supplies have to be paid for. 

Do you have a proposal, a solution?

Physicians cannot deduct non-collectible debt on tax returns. 
The government doesn’t pay physicians to take care of the uninsured, and neither does the NYT. 

The article is a mindless political hit on a physician who have given so much to his patients.
